title: The stylesheet had an unclosed rule, so everything after it was dropped
detail: assets/style.css line 601 opened `.pdp-art img{...}` and never closed it: the following @media(max-width:1000px) rule was swallowed into the declaration block. A CSS parser recovers at the next `}`, which silently discarded the responsive rule it contained. Found by brace-counting the file, not by reading the page. The brace and the missing `.hero`, `.hero-photo`, `.hero-copy`, `.hero-facts`, `.router*`, `.flip*`, `.aisle-photo` and `.pdp-photo` rules are now present, and scripts/check_site.py fails on an unbalanced stylesheet or on any class the generator emits that has no rule.
owner_status: Corrected in the generator's stylesheet; a gate rule now fails the build if the CSS stops parsing.

title: Guide read times were typed in, not measured
detail: Every guide kicker on the published site asserted a fixed read time (4 to 7 minutes) that had no relation to the copy underneath it: the shortest guide was 380 words and claimed 6 minutes. Nothing checked the figure, because nothing was expected to. Read time is now computed at build from the page's own visible words at 225 words per minute, rounded up, and scripts/check_site.py recomputes it from the rendered page and fails if the stated minutes are inconsistent. The stale literals in the seasonal module's kickers were removed so a regenerated guide cannot print a number that its own text contradicts.
owner_status: Corrected; the figure is derived from the copy, not authored alongside it.

title: Internal register codes were printed inside buyer-facing sentences
detail: Flag identifiers and crawl citations (FLG-007, FLG-022, FLG-036, 'chunk 7', 'intent record') appeared in image captions, product-card trade-off lines, comparison-table cells, guide standfirsts and the search index. They are true, but they are production notes, and a reader deciding what to buy should not have to decode a filing system to get the caveat. The substance now stays in plain language and the code appears only on audit surfaces, with each product page keeping a full record table under its own heading. The gate fails if an FLG code or a chunk citation is visible on any shop or guide page.
owner_status: Corrected on every reader page; flagged.html, sources.html and verification.html still carry all 55.

title: Pages printed their own markup: double-escaped entities in reader copy
detail: Guide fields that the renderer escapes (title, standfirst, intro, verdict) had been authored with HTML entity markup, so the escaping pass double-encoded them and readers saw the markup itself: thermometer-accuracy.html showed a visible plusmn entity where the sentence means plus-or-minus half a degree, and the first-week and Thanksgiving guides each showed a stray mdash entity. The page source looked correct, so this was found by reading the built pages rather than the registers. Fixed in the generator: escaped reader fields decode named and numeric entities to characters before escaping, all pages rebuilt clean, and the gate now unescapes every page's visible text and fails on any entity sequence left.
owner_status: Corrected; the gate rule covers all pages, not only the three that were visibly wrong.

title: P-04 accuracy claim and in-box certificate are still seller statements, not verified facts
detail: The listing for the ThermoMaven 1 Sec (B0DHZTCNR5) states an accuracy of plus or minus 0.5 degrees F, a 0.1 degree display resolution, and lists a calibration certificate among the contents. None of that has been confirmed against a manufacturer document or a test, and the USDA FSIS factsheet notes only that most thermometers are accurate within 2 to 4 degrees F, which is a baseline for the category rather than a judgement on this unit. The site publishes the figure as the seller's claim, attributed and dated, and the ice-water test guide explains how to check it on your own unit. No page calls it verified.
owner_status: Open; needs the manufacturer specification sheet or the certificate itself to move.
